judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section bears the number 6.6, duplicating the preceding compensation section, and "Unless otherwise restricted by Law" is an open qualifier; the removal right itself is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Sections 5.5(ii) and 6.1 (each Member elects and fills vacancies for its own Director), so the substance is coherent even though the numbering is not.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple agency statement bounded by "powers set forth in this Agreement".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to Section 7.6 for Officers and limited by Section 6.8; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Item (iii) is a fragment ("the declaration or making of any distributions to Members other than to reimburse DMSA for initial capital contributions") that reads as a substantive carve-out smuggled into a procedural list, and "material" in (viii) and (xiv) is undefined; the sub-numbering is corrupted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item (iii) cannot easily be reconciled with Section 9.1 (distributions in proportion to Percentage Interests), Section 4.3(i) (returns of capital only with all Members' consent and pro rata) or Section 9.2 (Board sets amounts) — a genuine whole-instrument problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and conventional officer provisions; "until their successors are chosen and qualify" is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Board-fixed salaries here sit against Section 6.8(x), which requires unanimous Board authorisation for employment contracts with Officers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "General and active management of the business" is a broad grant, but the execution authority is carefully bounded by exceptions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The President's contracting power is cut back by Section 6.8's unanimous-Board list and by Section 6.1's vesting of management in the Board, so the layers must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard succession clause with an express ordering rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-referenced by Section 7.2; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed enumeration of duties with no vague operative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the "Secretary" definition and the Schedule A updating duty in Section 2.1(iii); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional treasurer duties, determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Article X's books-and-records regime and Section 6.8(xi) on deposit banks.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short agency statement bounded by conferred powers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 6.7; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Fiduciary duty of loyalty and care similar to those of directors and officers of business corporations" imports an entire body of law by an undefined comparator ("similar to"), and the opening "Except to the extent provided herein" leaves the carve-out unspecified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 12.3 and 12.7 pull the other way — the latter expressly relieves DMSA of fiduciary duties as a Director and lets it compete — so the Agreement both imposes and disclaims loyalty duties.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two symmetrical sentences allocating by Percentage Interests; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.3(ii)(b) instead says profits are paid "in accordance with their respective Membership Interests", an undefined and possibly different measure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (ii) refers to how the Members "shared Interest Profits and Losses", which is garbled, and the sub-numbering repeats "(i)".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The intent-to-comply language in (iv) coexists with Section 15.3's Capital-Account liquidation and Section 8.1's Percentage-Interest allocations without direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard §704(c) provision; determinate by reference to tax law.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.1, 4.4 and 8.2(iv).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single clear rule of proportionality with an express Article XV carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8(iii) permits distributions only to reimburse DMSA absent unanimous approval, and Section 4.3(ii)(b) uses "Membership Interests", so the distribution scheme is not fully harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence conferring unfettered timing and amount discretion on the Board; brevity, not ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Board's discretion overlaps the Members' reserve-setting power in the Net Cash Flow definition and is constrained by Section 6.8(iii)'s unanimity, leaving who actually controls distributions unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward legal-compliance limitation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.3(i)'s parallel restriction on returns of capital.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Dense but conventional withholding language; "pursuant to this 9.4" drops the word "Section" without consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Article XI's tax provisions and Section 9.1; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires the books be kept "in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles ... and, to the extent inconsistent therewith, in accordance with this Agreement", and refers to "the Certificate", a term this Agreement never defines (it defines "Articles").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The undefined "Certificate" mismatches the "Articles" definition, and the GAAP requirement interacts with the cash-basis Net Cash Flow definition and accrual-basis Section 10.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mandate of the accrual method "for both financial and tax reporting purposes and for purposes of determining Profits and Losses" is clear on its own terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts the "Net Cash Flow" definition, which requires determination "in accordance with the cash receipts and disbursements method of accounting" — the two accounting mandates cannot both govern the same books.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Designation and a ten-day notice duty; both precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 11.2's partnership treatment and Section 1.1's cross-reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-sentence tax election statement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supports Sections 8.1-8.3 and 11.1; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard limited-liability shield, precisely bounded by "solely by reason of being a Member or Manager".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.4, 12.5 and 15.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text visibly breaks off mid-provision: after clause (i) it jumps to "professional or expert competence and who has been selected with reasonable care", so the reliance-on-advisors clause has lost its subject and operative verb.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The surviving fragment about facts "pertinent to the existence and amount of assets from which distributions to Members might properly be paid" relates to Sections 9.1-9.3 but cannot be tied to any grammatical rule in this section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The last sentence purports to "replace" all duties existing at law or equity "to the extent that they restrict" them, without specifying which provisions do the restricting — a self-referential and open-ended formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.7 expressly imposes corporate-style duties of loyalty and care on Directors and Officers, and Section 12.7 abrogates DMSA's; the three cannot be read together without a court choosing among them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but carefully bounded indemnity with express good-faith and gross-negligence limits, of the kind that rarely yields a construction fight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coherent with Sections 12.2, 12.5 and 12.6 and with the broad "Covered Person" definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mandatory advancement subject to an undertaking; clear, though the sentence ends without a period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Keyed correctly to Section 12.4 and payable out of Company assets under Section 12.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision stops mid-sentence at "against any liability that may be asserted", so the scope of insurable liability is simply missing from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Insurance is permissive and consistent with Sections 12.4 and 3.2(i)(h); the defect is textual rather than relational.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence is broken ("and the Company the income or profits derived therefrom"), and the LSB restriction turns on undefined vagaries — "diligent efforts", "such services", "to the extent it relates to the business" — in a provision drafted wholly in one party's favour.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relieves DMSA of "its fiduciary duties as a Director" although DMSA is a Member, contradicting Section 7.7's imposition of loyalty duties and sitting against Sections 12.3 and 3.1's statement of the Company's purpose.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The consent required is that of "the LLC", a term never defined or used elsewhere, the confidentiality obligation has no time limit, and the Proprietary Information list ends in an unbounded catch-all ("documents and data").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps Section 12.7's exclusivity/competition arrangement, under which DMSA may compete while holding the same information, a tension the confidentiality clause never addresses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Admission mechanics are precise: unanimous approval, execution, and naming on Schedule A.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.3 lets a transferee become a party merely by written undertaking, which does not obviously satisfy this unanimity requirement — a small gap between the two routes to membership.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Their respective Interest of the Company's income" is garbled, but the §706(d) machinery is otherwise conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article VIII's allocation rules and the Fiscal Year definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Without complying with the terms of this Agreement" is circular: the section prohibits assignment by reference to unspecified terms elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The actual restrictions live in Article XVI, yet Section 14.2 voids assignments "in violation of this Article XIV", so the operative prohibition and its enforcement sit in different Articles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear voiding rule and liability shield on its own terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It voids only assignments violating "this Article XIV", leaving transfers violating the Article XVI restrictions (16.2, 16.5, 16.6) without this sanction — an evident mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single flat prohibition requiring all Members' prior written consent; nothing vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.8 lets the Board alone waive "any transfer restrictions contained in this Agreement", which would override the Members' unanimous-consent right stated here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements Section 15.2's dissolution triggers and Section 13.1; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list is specific, but "retirement" and "expulsion" appear without any provision elsewhere creating them, and the trailing catch-all is tied to "any other event under the Maine Act".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (ii) treats a Member's "resignation" as a dissolution event although Section 5.4 flatly forbids resignation, and in this two-member LLC the "all of the remaining Members agree in writing" cure would rest with one holder.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The Members shall continue to distribute Interest Profits and Losses" is garbled, and "a reasonable time ... for the orderly liquidation" is an open-ended standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Liquidating proceeds go by Capital Account balances, whereas Sections 8.1 and 9.1 distribute by Percentage Interests, and Schedule A's contribution figures make the two measures diverge sharply.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise two-condition termination test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.3 and 15.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear exculpatory recourse limitation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aligns with Sections 12.1 and 4.5; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Making transfers effective "on Schedule A" and treating the Schedule as conclusive of ownership is clear if unusual.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Secretary alone updates Schedule A under Section 2.1(iii), which combined with this deeming rule could allow record ownership to move without the Section 16.6 or 13.1 protections.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of "transfer" is expansive with one carve-out, and the section promises restrictions "set forth below" without identifying them; the sanctions (no vote, no distribution) are, however, precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "restrictions ... set forth below" span Sections 16.3-16.6 and overlap Article XIV's prohibitions, and Section 16.8 lets the Board waive them all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two clear alternative conditions for a valid transfer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Becoming "a party to this Agreement" is not the same as admission as a Member under Section 13.1, which requires approval of all Members — the two provisions leave a transferee's status unsettled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is a truncated fragment ending "the Company and the other Members shall" — the operative obligation is entirely missing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to transfers "pursuant to Sections 16.9, 16.10, and 16.11", none of which exist in this Agreement (Article XVI ends at 16.8), a phantom cross-reference the instrument cannot cure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "In form and substance Satisfactory to the Board or the President" and waiver "for good cause" are both open-ended discretionary standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The President's power to waive here sits oddly with Section 16.8, which vests waiver of transfer restrictions in the Board acting by resolution.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to "the number of LLC Votes", a term never defined (the defined term is "Member Votes"), and the allocation sentence ("If the aggregate Interests offered to be purchased exceeds the number to be transferred") is confused about which quantity exceeds which.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The right of first refusal must be read with Sections 14.1, 16.2, 16.3 and 16.5, and Section 16.8 permits the Board to waive it outright; the interlocking timetable (90 days plus 60 days) is not tied back to those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permissive rule-making power expressly bounded by consistency with the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits alongside Section 16.8's waiver power; no contradiction identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary" plus a best-interests test gives the Board an unbounded waiver discretion, though the wording itself is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It empowers the Board to override restrictions that Sections 14.3 and 13.1 place in the hands of all Members unanimously — a direct allocation-of-power conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Methods of delivery are enumerated and the deemed-receipt rule is explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Notices to the Company go to the Section 2.5 address, which the Board may change unilaterally, and no notice address is given for the Company's officers; a minor loose end only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The double-negative construction ("shall not prevent a subsequent act ... from having the effect of an original violation") is convoluted and the final phrase is capitalised oddly, but the anti-waiver sense is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 17.3's cumulative-remedies clause; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard cumulative-remedies boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforces Section 17.2; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short binding-effect clause with an internal limitation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "to the extent permitted by this Agreement" qualifier defers correctly to Articles XIV and XVI on assigns.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional gender/number and cross-reference construction rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its promise that references correspond to provisions of this Agreement is undercut by the phantom references to Sections 6.9 and 16.9-16.11, though that failing belongs to those sections.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard severability wording; the stray period mid-sentence is immaterial.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision conditions the Agreement's validity on any particular clause surviving.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary counterparts clause, determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Sections 2.1(ii) and 13.1, which contemplate execution of counterparts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Pertaining to the subject matter hereof" leaves the superseded field undefined, which is the usual battleground for integration clauses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.7's service and exclusivity undertakings blur the line between this operating agreement and any employment or compensation arrangement that this clause would supersede.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Single choice-of-law sentence expressly excluding conflicts principles.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Maine Act references throughout; the Massachusetts location of the business does not create an internal conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires both an affirmative vote of all Members and a writing executed by all; clear if slightly redundant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(iii) lets the Secretary revise Schedule A — which fixes Percentage Interests and Member Votes — and declares such revisions not amendments, an evident route around this unanimity requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short no-third-party-beneficiary clause; the exception for "Members and Managers" is defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Covered Persons under Sections 12.2-12.5 include employees and agents who are neither Members nor Managers, yet this clause denies them rights — a mild internal tension.
